question: Do text-to-image models bind each prompt word to one resolved semantic role, or do ambiguous concepts and attributes leak across multiple depicted entities?

key_findings.claim: DALL-E 2 frequently renders both mutually exclusive senses of a homonym in one image.
key_findings.evidence: Across 17 hand-built stimuli and 12 outputs per stimulus, 80.3% of 216 images display homonym duplication, such as both a flying mammal and baseball bat. Most words need context favoring the normally dispreferred sense; only 'bass' and 'date' reliably duplicate without added context.

anchors.section: A single word realized as multiple entities

key_findings.claim: A modifier syntactically attached to one noun often colors or shapes another compatible noun as well.
key_findings.evidence: For six challenge-control pairs, 97.2% of challenge images show the shared property versus 15.2% of minimally altered controls. The prompt 'a fish and a gold ingot,' for example, commonly produces a golden fish even though 'gold' modifies 'ingot.'

anchors.section: A single word realized as a modifier of multiple entities

key_findings.claim: An entity word can simultaneously appear as an object and leak an associated visual property onto another object.
key_findings.evidence: Across ten challenge-control pairs, 92.5% of challenge outputs share the associated property versus 6.6% of controls. Examples include a zebra inducing a striped crosswalk, a seal inducing a sealed letter, or 'cone' inducing ice-cream-cone food while also denoting a hat shape.

anchors.section: A single word realized as entity and modifier

key_findings.claim: Leakage can be triggered by a description of an unspoken concept, suggesting concept-level rather than literal token copying.
key_findings.evidence: The phrase 'a tall, long-legged, long-necked bird and a construction site' can yield both bird and construction cranes and blend their shapes despite never saying 'crane.' The minimally different 'a bird and a construction site' control does not show the same behavior.

key_findings.claim: The reported percentages are descriptive evidence for selected failure probes, not prevalence estimates for ordinary use.
key_findings.evidence: Prompts were manually constructed to surface the clearest failures, sample sizes are small, and the paper does not specify blinded raters, annotation rules, inter-rater agreement, API/version/seed controls, confidence intervals, or hypothesis tests. The authors explicitly say random outputs usually look good and call for automatic large-scale stimulus generation.

key_findings.claim: The study localizes neither the cause nor model-generality of the phenomenon.
key_findings.evidence: DALL-E 2 is a closed commercial system, so the text encoder and decoder cannot be intervened on. Preliminary DALL-E mini and Stable Diffusion checks show less duplication but are not quantified; the paper hypothesizes that worse prompt following masks the failure and leaves architecture/scale dependence for future work.

method.core_idea: Use targeted linguistic minimal pairs to expose violations of word-sense resolution and object-attribute binding in generated images.
method.mechanism: Construct three prompt families: homonyms whose senses are jointly plausible in context, modifiers compatible with two nouns but syntactically attached to one, and entity nouns visually associated with a property of another noun. Generate 12 DALL-E 2 images per prompt, compare challenge prompts with hand-designed minimally different controls, and manually aggregate whether both senses or leaked properties appear. Add second-order prompts that describe rather than name the ambiguous concept.
assumptions: The proposed single-role-per-symbol principle is the right operational target for the tested syntactic configurations.
Challenge and control prompts differ only in the causal trigger of interest rather than plausibility, visual prior, or prompt specificity.
Manual judgments of duplication and property leakage are reliable despite no documented annotation protocol.
Twelve API samples per selected prompt adequately represent DALL-E 2's conditional output distribution.
Observed images reveal representational binding errors rather than stochastic decoding coincidences or dataset co-occurrence priors.

techniques.role: Tests whether an ambiguous token is resolved to one sense or rendered in semantic superposition.
Estimates how often a target property appears without the hypothesized leakage trigger.
Tests whether syntax confines an attribute to its intended object.
Tests whether one depicted noun also acts as a visual modifier of another.
Separates concept activation from literal repetition of an ambiguous word.
Measures stochastic failure frequency over twelve generations per stimulus.

evaluations.setting: Seventeen context-augmented homonym prompts, twelve DALL-E 2 outputs each.
evaluations.metric: Fraction of images depicting both incompatible senses.
evaluations.result: 80.3% of 216 images are labeled as homonym duplication.
evaluations.baseline: Qualitative comparison to uncontextualized homonym prompts; no systematic model baseline.

evaluations.metric: Fraction of outputs in which the attribute is shared by the syntactically unmodified entity.
evaluations.baseline: Minimally changed prompt intended to disable the leakage association.

evaluations.setting: Ten entity-as-modifier challenge/control pairs plus descriptive second-order cases.
evaluations.metric: Fraction of images displaying the associated property on the second entity and qualitative concept blending.
evaluations.result: 92.5% for challenges versus 6.6% for controls; unnamed concepts can also trigger duplication.
evaluations.baseline: Hand-designed controls replacing or specifying one noun.

limitations: The manually curated stimuli were selected to elicit the effect, so aggregate rates cannot estimate natural-prompt incidence.
No blinded annotation protocol, multiple-rater agreement, raw per-image labels, statistical intervals, or inferential tests are reported.
DALL-E 2 is closed and versioned externally, preventing mechanism attribution and exact longitudinal reproduction.
Challenge and control prompts may differ in frequency, specificity, or real-world plausibility as well as the intended leakage trigger.
Other models receive only preliminary qualitative checks, with prompt adherence confounded with absence of leakage.
The paper does not test whether text-encoder representations, cross-attention, data co-occurrence, or decoder dynamics cause each failure.
The linguistic single-use framing does not itself supply a complete theory of legitimate shared modification, ellipsis, polysemy, or visual metaphor.
failure_modes: An automatic evaluator confuses correct compound objects such as goldfish with leaked color attributes.
A control removes leakage only because it makes the scene less natural or causes the model to ignore an object.
New model/API versions change the phenomenon, making the fixed image audit obsolete.
Explicit prompt disambiguation suppresses duplication but reduces diversity or overrides intended creative ambiguity.
Object co-occurrence priors, not token reuse, explain apparent leakage, so an intervention aimed only at attention binding fails.
A model improves benchmark binding through evaluator gaming while still failing on long-tail words and natural syntax.
reusable_insights: Test compositional generators with causal minimal pairs rather than global CLIP similarity alone.
Separate object presence, attribute presence, and correct object-attribute assignment in evaluation.
Ambiguous tokens are adversarially useful probes of whether a conditioning representation resolves meaning before generation.
Descriptions of an unstated concept can distinguish concept-level superposition from literal token duplication.
Benchmark prompt following jointly with binding so a model cannot look better merely by ignoring difficult prompt content.
For stochastic APIs, archive exact outputs, timestamps, model versions, sampling settings, and per-output annotations.
open_questions: Does homonym duplication originate in contextual text embeddings, cross-attention, the denoising dynamics, or training-data correlations?
How prevalent are these failures in naturally occurring multilingual prompts under representative user distributions?
Can syntax-aware conditioning fix binding without sacrificing image quality, diversity, or legitimate shared modifiers?
How should automatic VLM judges be calibrated against humans for rare senses and subtle attribute leakage?
Do larger and newer diffusion/flow models resolve ambiguity or simply hide duplication through stronger default priors?
Can uncertainty over intended sense be surfaced to users rather than silently collapsed or superposed?

competitive_landscape.title: Schrodinger's Bat: Diffusion Models Sometimes Generate Polysemous Words in Superposition
competitive_landscape.difference: White and Cotterell replicate homonym duplication in Stable Diffusion, show summed concept embeddings produce both objects, and linearly edit CLIP representations to control word sense. This directly advances the target from behavioral discovery toward an encoder-superposition mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: T2I-CompBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Open-world Compositional Text-to-image Generation
competitive_landscape.difference: T2I-CompBench scales composition tests to 6,000 prompts spanning color, shape, texture, spatial and non-spatial relations, validates automatic metrics, and adds reward-based fine-tuning. The target isolates subtler homonym and association leakage with stronger hand-crafted causal probes but far narrower coverage.

competitive_landscape.title: Attend-and-Excite: Attention-Based Semantic Guidance for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Attend-and-Excite modifies latent variables so every subject token receives sufficient attention, reducing catastrophic subject neglect without retraining. It addresses missing concepts more than the target's wrong binding or homonym superposition and can still attend to the wrong entity.

competitive_landscape.title: Object-Attribute Binding in Text-to-Image Generation: Evaluation and Control
competitive_landscape.difference: Trusca et al. build an image-graph alignment evaluator and use syntactic structure to disentangle CLIP embeddings and focus cross-attention on the intended object. This operationalizes a mechanism and mitigation for the target's modifier-leakage cases, though not necessarily ambiguous word senses.

competitive_landscape.title: Un-Doubling Diffusion: LLM-guided Disambiguation of Homonym Duplication
competitive_landscape.difference: Kaskov et al. automate duplication measurement with VLM and human evaluation across models and reduce it through LLM prompt expansion, including homonyms introduced by English translation. It directly scales and mitigates the target phenomenon while introducing dependence on judge and rewrite quality.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims that DALL-E 2 violates a basic single-role mapping between prompt symbols and depicted concepts through homonym duplication and concept leakage.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Three hand-built stimulus families yield reported challenge rates of 80.3%, 97.2%, and 92.5%, with strong drops in minimal controls and qualitative second-order examples.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The taxonomy and minimal-pair demonstrations are memorable, falsifiable early evidence that global image-text quality hides binding failures. Novelty lies in isolating word-sense and cross-entity reuse, not in a broad benchmark or causal mechanism; the selected prompts and undocumented scoring sharply limit prevalence claims.

reviewer_notes: Read all 13 cached pages, including OCR-recovered prompt tables and image appendices. Competitors were checked from primary arXiv/OpenReview records through 2025 on 2026-08-23. Percentages are transcribed as author-reported and explicitly not interpreted as population prevalence.
